general.title: How to do the exercises
examples: how do I do the exercises
what is the correct way to do this exercise
how do I know my form is right
can you explain the steps
general.answer: Open the exercise in your plan to see its steps and safety points. Move slowly and smoothly, and record yourself so the app can check your posture and give you tips.

general.title: Pain or discomfort
examples: my knee hurts when I exercise
is it normal to feel sore after exercising
what should I do if I feel pain
my muscles ache the next day
general.answer: Mild muscle tiredness or soreness for a day or two is normal when you start. Sharp pain, or pain that gets worse during an exercise, is not: stop that exercise and rest. If the pain lasts more than a few days, contact your doctor or physiotherapist before continuing.

general.title: How often to exercise
examples: how often should I exercise
can I do this every day
how many times a week
how long should each session be
general.answer: Follow the number of sessions per week shown in your plan, with a rest day in between when you can. Your reminders are set to match this schedule. Quality matters more than doing extra sessions.

general.title: Missed a session
examples: I missed my session yesterday
what if I skip a day
I forgot to exercise
general.answer: That is fine. Do your next session as usual; do not do two sessions in one day to catch up. If you miss several days, start again gently with fewer repetitions.

general.title: Exercising safely
examples: is it safe for me to exercise
how do I avoid falling
what if I feel dizzy
should I hold my breath
general.answer: Exercise near a stable chair or counter, on a non-slip floor, and breathe normally; do not hold your breath. Stop if you feel dizzy, short of breath or unwell. Your plan already respects the safety limits from your health profile.

general.title: What you need
examples: what equipment do I need
do I need weights
what kind of chair should I use
what should I wear
general.answer: Most exercises only need a firm chair without wheels, pushed against a wall. Floor exercises need a mat, and step-ups need a low step with a rail. Wear comfortable clothes and non-slip shoes. A light water bottle can be used as a weight if your plan says so.

categories.title: Progress and results
examples: when will I see results
how do I know I am improving
is the plan working
what happens when I finish this plan
categories.answer: This plan aims to help you move your joints more freely. Most people notice a difference after two to four weeks of regular sessions. Your progress bar moves forward each time you complete an exercise with good posture; when the plan is complete, ask for a new recommendation to move on.
